thread.title: Fitbit Doubles Down on Smartwatches With Two New Products

author: thestreet.com
title: Fitbit Doubles Down on Smartwatches With Two New Products
text:
Watch out, Apple ( AAPL ) Watch?
After releasing its first full-fledged smartwatch in 2017, Fitbit Inc. ( FIT ) announced two new smartwatch products on Tuesday, the Fitbit Versa and the Fitbit Ace, as it tries to broaden its scope beyond basic fitness trackers.
In its fourth-quarter earnings call in February, CEO James Park said that the company's fitness performance-focused smartwatch, the Fitbit Ionic, did not have enough of a mass appeal or competitive price point to fare as well as other competitors in the smartwatch market. The Ionic lists for $299.95.
For the quarter, Fitbit missed estimates and guided for additional losses and a big drop in earnings in early 2018, causing shares to plunge 12% the day after the report.
Fitbit's new products target a new audience and offer more competitive price points, according to the company's announcements. The Fitbit Versa is a lightweight smartwatch that will be released in April for $199.95, while the Fitbit Ace is the company's first activity tracker for children. The Ace is designed for kids 8 years old and older and will launch in May for $99.95.
Fitbit also announced that Fitbit OS 2.0 will accompany the release of the Versa in April; the OS will offer new apps with features such as women's health tracking tools.
Stifel analyst Jim Duffy wrote on Tuesday that the new products look "well-conceived" for price-conscious consumers and children. But he added that "with category units looking for stabilization and the concession in ASP [average selling price], we don't yet see a path to revenue stabilization." Duffy maintained his hold rating and $5.50 target price on the stock.
On Wednesday afternoon, Fitbit shares were down 0.6% at $5.36. Since the beginning of the year, the stock has dropped 6.1%.
